title: Implement Trie Prefix Tree
description:
Store lowercase words by their characters so exact words and prefixes can be queried separately.

Implement the Trie class:

  • __init__() creates an empty trie.
  • insert(word: str) -> None stores word as a complete word; inserting it again has no extra effect.
  • search(word: str) -> bool returns true only when word was inserted as a complete word.
  • startsWith(prefix: str) -> bool returns true when at least one stored word begins with prefix.

A path that exists only because a longer word was inserted is not by itself a complete word. An empty prefix matches even an empty trie; words and search queries are nonempty.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls on one live object. The first call names the class and passes constructor arguments; subsequent calls name methods and their arguments. The constructor and methods returning nothing report null; the result array has one entry per call.

Constraints:

  • Words and search queries contain 1 to 200 lowercase English letters.
  • Prefixes contain 0 to 200 lowercase English letters.
  • At most 30000 calls.

Example 1:

Calls: ["Trie","insert","search","search","startsWith","insert","search"]
Arguments: [[],["apple"],["apple"],["app"],["app"],["app"],["app"]]
Output: [null,null,true,false,true,null,true]

The prefix app exists before insertion, but is only a complete word afterward.

Example 2:

Calls: ["Trie","startsWith","search","insert","startsWith","search"]
Arguments: [[],[""],["a"],["at"],["a"],["at"]]
Output: [null,true,false,null,true,true]

The empty prefix always exists; a is not an inserted word.

Example 3:

Calls: ["Trie","insert","insert","search","startsWith","search"]
Arguments: [[],["car"],["cat"],["ca"],["ca"],["cat"]]
Output: [null,null,null,false,true,true]

Both words share ca, but ca was never inserted.
